claims.text: YouTrack offers a free plan for up to 10 users on both Cloud and Server editions.
claims.evidence: Independent developers and small teams can continue using the free YouTrack Cloud plan, which includes support for up to 10 users.

claims.text: YouTrack paid monthly plans start at $5.40 per user.
claims.evidence: For monthly plans, the new pricing starts at USD 5.40 per user per month.

claims.text: YouTrack paid annual plans start at $4.50 per user per month.
claims.evidence: If you prefer an annual subscription, you’ll get two months free – the new starting price will be USD 4.50 per user per month.

claims.text: One source lists YouTrack pricing starting at $3.67 per user per month.
claims.evidence: The pricing for Jetbrains Youtrack starts at $3.67 per user per month.

claims.text: A team of 10 users pays roughly $50 per month, or about $600 per year.
claims.evidence: For 10 users, the monthly cost is around $50, translating to approximately $600 annually.

claims.text: A team of 100 users pays roughly $500 per month, or about $6,000 per year.
claims.evidence: Scaling to 100 users would cost about $500 per month or $6,000 per year.

claims.text: YouTrack implementation for small and midsize businesses can cost a few hundred dollars, while enterprise implementation ranges from $5,000 to $50,000.
claims.evidence: For enterprises, implementation, customization, training, and migration can range from $5,000 to $50,000 depending on complexity.

claims.text: YouTrack HelpDesk includes three support agent seats at no extra charge; additional cloud agents cost $6 per month each.
claims.evidence: For cloud-based HelpDesk users, the add-on remains free for the first three agents. For larger support teams, each additional agent seat is priced at $6 per month.

claims.text: For self-hosted YouTrack Server, additional HelpDesk agents beyond the included three cost $72 per year each.
claims.evidence: Beyond this, each additional agent seat is priced at $72 per year.

claims.text: YouTrack uses volume pricing where the per-user cost decreases as more users are added.
claims.evidence: The larger your team, the lower your price, thanks to discount increasing as you add users.

claims.text: Jira Standard plan pricing starts at $7.91 per user per month and Premium at $14.54 per user per month.
claims.evidence: Jira pricing starts at $7.91 per user, per month for the Standard plan and $14.54 per user, per month for the Premium version, for up to 300 users.

claims.text: Jira offers a free plan for up to 10 users.
claims.evidence: A free version is available for small teams or individual users with up to 10 users.

claims.text: Linear Basic costs $10 per user per month and Business costs $16 per user per month with yearly billing.
claims.evidence: As of July 2026, Basic runs $10 per user/month and Business runs $16 per user/month, both billed yearly, while the free plan is genuinely usable for small teams — unlimited members, but capped at 2 teams and 250 issues.

claims.text: Linear offers a free plan capped at two teams and 250 issues.
claims.evidence: As of July 2026, Basic runs $10 per user/month and Business runs $16 per user/month, both billed yearly, while the free plan is genuinely usable for small teams — unlimited members, but capped at 2 teams and 250 issues.

claims.text: GitLab Premium is listed at $29 per user per month by one source. (price check unavailable)
Another source lists GitLab Premium at roughly $32 per user per year.
claims.evidence: Premium Plan: €29/user/year (~$32) — Best value for growing teams

claims.text: GitLab Ultimate is listed at roughly $108 per user per year.
claims.evidence: Ultimate Plan: €99/user/year (~$108) — Enterprise with advanced security

claims.text: YouTrack is a developer-focused issue tracker built by the same company that creates IntelliJ, WebStorm, and PyCharm.
claims.evidence: YouTrack is JetBrains' issue tracker, and if you're already paying for IntelliJ, WebStorm, or PyCharm, it's worth a serious look.

claims.text: One reviewer describes YouTrack as feeling like it was designed by developers frustrated with Jira.
claims.evidence: It's developer-opinionated in a way that feels like it was designed by developers who were frustrated with Jira.

claims.text: YouTrack bundles Scrum and Kanban boards, sprint planning with dependencies, time tracking, a Gantt chart, 20 configurable reports and dashboards, a knowledge base, and helpdesk projects.
claims.evidence: YouTrack puts in one product much of what Linear leaves to other tools: Scrum and Kanban boards, sprint planning with dependencies, time tracking, a Gantt chart, 20 configurable reports and dashboards, a knowledge base, and helpdesk projects that turn email or a web form into tickets.

claims.text: YouTrack includes JetBrains AI for writing assistance, summaries, and converting text into issues.
claims.evidence: JetBrains AI helps with writing, summaries and turning text into issues.

claims.text: YouTrack Cloud is free with all features for up to 10 users, and a self-hosted Server edition is available.
claims.evidence: The cloud edition is free with every feature for up to 10 users, larger teams pay per user at a rate that falls with size, and a Server edition can be self-hosted.

claims.text: YouTrack is denser and more configurable than Linear, which can demand more from users.
claims.evidence: The trade-off: it is a denser, more configurable tool than Linear, so it asks more of whoever sets it up.

claims.text: One reviewer selected YouTrack because its AI features are deeper than those of most issue trackers, highlighting a Text-to-Issue Transformation capability.
claims.evidence: I picked YouTrack because its AI features go deeper than what most issue trackers offer.

claims.text: YouTrack is positioned as best for mid-size and large development teams needing customizable workflows and advanced issue management.
claims.evidence: Mid-size and large development teams that need customizable workflows and advanced issue management across software projects.

claims.text: YouTrack supports backlog automation that automatically brings issues with a specified Fix version into the backlog.
claims.evidence: YouTrack's Fix version backlog lets teams configure a scrum board so that issues with a specified Fix version enter the backlog automatically, or add issues manually during sprint planning.

claims.text: YouTrack offers a sprint rollover feature via a Move to the next sprint button.
claims.evidence: Sprint rollover: Teams move unfinished items forward via YouTrack's "Move to the next sprint" button or planning view.

claims.text: YouTrack can require complex setup and has a steep learning curve for teams unfamiliar with custom workflow configuration.
claims.evidence: YouTrack requires complex setup for teams unfamiliar with custom workflow configuration.

claims.text: YouTrack provides agile boards with sprints and burndown charts, a query language, JavaScript workflow rules, time tracking, reports, and a helpdesk with a knowledge base.
claims.evidence: Where Redmine hands you a foundation, YouTrack hands you an assembled product: agile boards with sprints and burndown charts, a search-based query language, JavaScript workflow rules for automation, time tracking, reports, and a helpdesk with a knowledge base for teams that also field customer ticke

claims.text: YouTrack includes predefined import scripts for migrating data from Redmine, Jira, GitHub, Asana, ClickUp, and Mantis.
claims.evidence: It also ships a predefined import script for Redmine, alongside the Jira, GitHub, Asana, ClickUp and Mantis ones, which connects to your instance through its API instead of asking you to hand-prepare a file.

claims.text: Linear is considered faster than YouTrack and offers defaults that reduce team process debates, along with a smoother daily filing and triaging experience.
claims.evidence: Linear is better than YouTrack on speed, on defaults that stop teams debating process, and on the daily experience of filing and triaging work — which is what most of its users are buying.

claims.text: Jira is an enterprise agile project management platform with customizable workflows and issue tracking used inside and outside software teams.
claims.evidence: The solution features a customizable workflow, a multi-faceted issue-tracking system, and other features that help to streamline the management of complex projects.

claims.text: GitLab’s issue tracker is less configurable than YouTrack but integrates issues, merge requests, pipelines, and releases into one system.
claims.evidence: GitLab's issue tracker is not as configurable as YouTrack's, but it has one advantage nothing else here matches: issues, merge requests, pipelines, and releases are the same system.

claims.text: Atlassian is discontinuing Jira Server and datacenter products in favor of cloud-only offerings, with server support ending after February 15, 2024.
claims.evidence: Server support ends on Feb 15, 2024.

claims.text: A user review calls YouTrack a very complete product and notes appreciation for its depth.
claims.evidence: > "It is a very complete product, I appreciate the deep integration between the different part of the software."

claims.text: A reviewer chose YouTrack because its AI features are more extensive than those of most other issue trackers.
claims.evidence: I picked YouTrack because its AI features go deeper than what most issue trackers offer.

claims.text: One review indicates YouTrack can require complex setup and has a steep learning curve for teams unfamiliar with custom workflow configuration.
claims.evidence: YouTrack requires complex setup for teams unfamiliar with custom workflow configuration.
